correctness.rationale: The exact 30-vertex incidence graph decomposes into two independent 15-bit majority maps. Two separately constructed programs exhaust every one of the 32,768 possible states on BOTH shores and verify G^3=G^2 and J^3=J^2, with G^2 != G; both find 2,386 two-step-fixed symbols on each shore and the same five eligibility counts. The rigorous algebraic swap argument gives 2,386 fixed states and 2,845,305 primitive two-cycles, while independent exact phase-projection products yield the full five-by-two transient-period table summing to 2^30. A concrete duad-subset witness {13,15,23,24} with empty syntheme subset first enters recurrence at time four. The first checker also enumerates all 720 relabellings and 156 six-vertex graph classes, exactly 18 stable; the second explicitly reconstructs the 30-vertex graph, girth and bitwise neighbor votes. Both stored files ran successfully. The 12,032 global-state samples are supplementary checks, not an alleged exhaustive 2^30 loop.

evidence: Benjamini–Chan–O’Donnell–Tamuz–Tan (arXiv:1405.2486) records the general eventual period-two property on finite graphs; the inspected article analyzes infinite unimodular and random graph behavior, not an exact Tutte–Coxeter attractor portrait.

Kaaser–Mallmann-Trenn–Natale (arXiv:1508.03519; MFCS 2016 PDF) gives general upper bounds and computational complexity of voting times, not the precise 4-update cutoff or orbit/entrance populations of the cage.
Goles–Olivos (Discrete Math. 1980) proves eventual periods at most two for symmetric threshold maps, without providing graph-specific numbers in the accessible abstract.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general period-two conclusion does not imply this sharp time bound, the 2,386-symbol count, the 18 isomorphism classes, or any of the exact first-entry/period totals. General time bounds do not resolve the exact state counts.

value.rationale: The unique cubic girth-eight cage is an extremal graph with a canonical K6 edge/perfect-matching realization, making its full deterministic-majority portrait a natural rather than arbitrary finite invariant. A billion-state 30-vertex first-entry/period classification collapses to an exact 15-bit per-shore lemma, with a sharp four-update bound not implied by general period-two theory. The further 18 of 156 six-vertex graph shapes link the dynamics to classical graph-isomorphism structure. This supplies a meaningful finite benchmark and a qualitatively different incidence-projection depth from the Heawood case, without claiming an infinite-family theorem.
